items.name: Eohostimella heathana
items.basis: Spinose, dichotomously branching tubular compressions lack known reproductive organs and diagnostic vascular anatomy. Embryophyte identity remains unproved.
items.source: [Schopf et al. (1966), Erect plants in the early Silurian of Maine](https://pubs.usgs.gov/pp/0550d/report.pdf)

items.name: Eophyllophyton bellum
items.basis: Pseudomonopodial branching, divided appendages and terminal sporangial trusses support basal euphyllophyte affinity. Its placement on the euphyllophyte stem still places it within crown Tracheophyta.
items.source: [Clarke et al. (2011), Establishing a time-scale for plant evolution](https://nph.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/j.1469-8137.2011.03794.x)

items.name: Eorhynia primigenia
items.basis: Eorhynia has smooth, occasionally dichotomising axes terminated by elongate sporangia. Anatomical preservation does not establish crown-tracheophyte membership.
items.source: [Edwards and Rogerson (1979), New records of fertile Rhyniophytina from the late Silurian of Wales](https://orca.cardiff.ac.uk/id/eprint/10902/1/Edwards%201979.pdf)

items.name: Eospermatopteris
items.basis: Trunks and bases assigned to Eospermatopteris are organically connected to Wattieza crowns, establishing cladoxylopsid affinity.
items.source: [Stein et al. (2007), Giant cladoxylopsid trees resolve the enigma of the Earth's earliest forest stumps at Gilboa](https://www.nature.com/articles/nature05705)

items.name: Estinnophyton gracile
items.basis: Estinnophyton bears divided fertile appendages carrying stalked sporangia and is interpreted as a primitive sphenopsid. The precise sphenopsid relationship is less secure than its broad euphyllophyte affinity.
items.source: [Hao, Wang and Wang (2004), A new species of Estinnophyton from the Lower Devonian Posongchong Formation, Yunnan, China](https://academic.oup.com/botlinnean/article-abstract/146/2/201/2420369)

items.name: Euphyllophytina
items.basis: This higher-group identification denotes the euphyllophyte lineage, sister to Lycophytina within crown vascular plants.
items.source: [Claisse et al. (2025), Re-evaluating the phylogenetic relationships of zosterophylls](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13274996/)

items.name: Flabellofolium
items.basis: Flabellofolium replaces Platyphyllum for isolated, large, fan-shaped leaves. Their parent plants and systematic relationships remain insufficiently resolved for a particular crown lineage.
items.source: [Snigirevsky and Lyubarova (2023), New fossil plant from the Late Devonian strata of Northern Timan](https://pureportal.spbu.ru/files/116919897/Snigirevsky_Lyubarova_2023.pdf)

items.name: Foozia minuta
items.basis: Branched axes bear slender lateral appendages terminating in paired sporangia, with vascular evidence supporting probable cladoxylopsid affinity.
items.source: [Gerrienne (1992), The Emsian plants from Fooz-Wépion: III. Foozia minuta, a new taxon with probable cladoxylalean affinities](https://orbi.uliege.be/handle/2268/101836)

items.name: Gilboaphyton
items.basis: Gilboaphyton is a herbaceous lycopsid with diagnostic leaf-base patterns and leaves bearing paired lateral teeth. The PBDB psilophyte grouping is misleading.
items.source: [Berry and Edwards (1997), A new species of the lycopsid Gilboaphyton from Venezuela and New York State](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0034666796000152)

items.name: Gosferia curvata
items.basis: A zosterophyll bearing reniform sporangia on long, abaxially recurved stalks. Gosferia is the replacement name for the preoccupied fossil genus Forgesia.
items.source: [Gerrienne (1999), Gosferia, a new name for Forgesia](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/271789417_Gosferia_a_new_name_for_Forgesia_fossil_plants)

items.name: Gosslingia
items.basis: A zosterophyll genus with branched axes, lateral sporangia and characteristic vascular anatomy.
items.source: [Edwards (1970), Further observations on the Lower Devonian plant Gosslingia breconensis](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22408827/)

items.name: Gosslingia breconensis
items.basis: Lateral sporangia, branched axes and anatomically documented xylem establish zosterophyll affinity.
items.source: [Kenrick and Edwards (1988), The anatomy of Lower Devonian Gosslingia breconensis based on pyritized axes](https://academic.oup.com/botlinnean/article-abstract/97/2/95/2660285)

items.name: Gumuia zyzzata
items.basis: Successive lateral and terminal sporangia form a distinctive zigzag fertile system. The original description tentatively assigns the plant to the zosterophylls.
items.source: [Hao (1989), Gumuia zyzzata, a new plant from the Lower Devonian of Yunnan](https://www.jipb.net/EN/abstract/abstract26800.shtml)

items.name: Haplostigma
items.basis: A lycopsid stem morphogenus characterised by regularly arranged appendage bases and surface patterns. The broad affinity is better established than individual species delimitations.
items.source: [Middle Devonian herbaceous lycopsid Haplostigma from the Paraná Basin (2015)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0016699515000601)

items.name: Harringtonia
items.basis: The supplied identification H. acutiplicata matches the Silurian brachiopod Harringtonina acutiplicata. A spelling or name-resolution collision probably explains its placement under cycads.
items.source: [Carrera et al. (2011), Silurian–Devonian coral associations across a sequence stratigraphic boundary in the Argentine Precordillera](https://ri.conicet.gov.ar/bitstream/handle/11336/24993/CONICET_Digital_Nro.78aff3b5-f870-4e52-81b1-f9ae865fa72f_A.pdf?sequence=2)

items.name: Haskinsia
items.basis: A herbaceous lycopsid with dichotomising stems and helically arranged, petiolate leaves. Fertile material documents adaxially attached sporangia.
items.source: [Berry and Edwards (1996), The herbaceous lycophyte Haskinsia from the Devonian of western Venezuela](https://orca.cardiff.ac.uk/id/eprint/10071/)

items.name: Haskinsia sagittata
items.basis: Sagittate leaves and sporangia attached adaxially to otherwise unmodified leaves establish herbaceous lycopsid affinity.
items.source: [Berry and Edwards (1996), The herbaceous lycophyte Haskinsia from the Devonian of western Venezuela](https://orca.cardiff.ac.uk/id/eprint/10071/)

items.name: Heidiphyllum
items.basis: Heidiphyllum denotes Triassic conifer foliage, far younger than this study interval. The clade flags describe that seed-plant affinity; the exceptionally broad collection age does not validate an early occurrence.
items.source: [Gnaedinger and colleagues, The fossil flora of the Huimpil-Llafquentué Formation, Upper Triassic, Chile](https://revista.macn.gov.ar/index.php/RevMus/article/view/90)

items.name: Hicklingia edwardi
items.basis: This denotes Hicklingia edwardii, whose sporangia were reinterpreted as lateral rather than terminal. That morphology supports provisional zosterophyll affinity.
items.source: [Edwards (1976), The systematic position of Hicklingia edwardii](https://orca.cardiff.ac.uk/id/eprint/10194/)

items.name: Horneophyton lignieri
items.basis: A branched sporophyte with columellate sporangia. Reinvestigation identifies conducting cells fundamentally different from tracheids and supports exclusion from Tracheophyta.
items.source: [Kenrick et al. (2026), Transfer cells in Horneophyton lignieri illuminate the origin of vascular tissues in land plants](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12917476/)

items.name: Hostinella
items.basis: A form genus for smooth, usually dichotomising sterile land-plant axes. Anatomy demonstrated in particular species cannot be transferred to every Hostinella identification.
items.source: [Edwards (1979), A late Silurian flora from the Lower Old Red Sandstone of south-west Dyfed](https://zenodo.org/records/15904054/files/bhlpart173475.pdf?download=1)

items.name: Howisonia
items.basis: Howisonia rara is based on a small sterile stem fragment with apparent filamentous foliage. Superficial lycopod resemblance does not establish a vascular lineage, and the Witpoort provenance needs finer age checking.
items.source: [Exploring biodiversity patterns among southern African Devonian plants, discussion of Howisonia rara](https://wiredspace.wits.ac.za/server/api/core/bitstreams/0eeb5f47-e296-4067-b3fa-0d43fc9f4306/content)

items.name: Huia recurvata
items.basis: Branched axes bear spikes of stalked, recurved lateral sporangia and a centrarch protostele. This unusual combination does not securely resolve lycophyte versus other early vascular-plant affinity.
items.source: [Geng (1985), Huia recurvata, a new plant from Lower Devonian southeastern Yunnan](https://www.jipb.net/EN/abstract/abstract26233.shtml)

items.name: Hunanodendrum typicum
items.basis: Originally described as a graptolite, Hunanodendrum is retained in a modern revision among fossils that cannot currently be assigned to a recognised group. No embryophyte identification is established.
items.source: [Maletz and Steiner (2021), Treatise Online 152: Uncertain genera](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/355267056_Treatise_Online_no_152_Part_V_Second_Revision_Chapter_29_Uncertain_genera)

items.name: Hyenia
items.basis: Revised fertile morphology places material called Hyenia elegans with cladoxylopsids, including Calamophyton. Historical uncertainty over generic limits does not alter that broad euphyllophyte affinity.
items.source: [Fairon-Demaret and Berry (2000), A reconsideration of Hyenia elegans and Hyenia complexa](https://orca.cardiff.ac.uk/id/eprint/10027/)

items.name: Isidrophyton iniguezii
items.basis: Repeatedly branching axes terminate in paired, sessile sporangia and show distinctive fusiform surface features. These establish polysporangiate organisation without securely resolving vascular anatomy or crown lineage.
items.source: [Edwards et al. (2001), Land plants in the Devonian Villavicencio Formation, Mendoza Province, Argentina](https://api.naturalis.fcnym.unlp.edu.ar/server/api/core/bitstreams/9242abeb-8b21-43e9-8183-b6db74f6efb9/content)

items.name: Jenisseiphyton
items.basis: Historical descriptions tentatively compare the genus with laminarian algae, whereas later accounts call J. rudnevae lycopod-like. The conflicting interpretations do not support a secure genus-wide assignment.
items.source: [Osnovy paleontologii (1963), algae and early land plants, p. 191](https://paleosamara.ru/wp-content/uploads/2022/01/osnovy-paleontologii-14-vodorosli-plaunovidnyje.pdf); [Tomsk University account discussing J. rudnevae](https://www.lib.tsu.ru/mminfo/000063105/353/image/353-205.pdf)

items.name: Jenisseiphyton lebedevii
items.basis: The historical treatment places this type species tentatively among Laminariales, without demonstrated reproductive organs or a vascular system. Its affinity remains insufficiently resolved.
items.source: [Osnovy paleontologii (1963), algae and early land plants, p. 191](https://paleosamara.ru/wp-content/uploads/2022/01/osnovy-paleontologii-14-vodorosli-plaunovidnyje.pdf)

items.name: Jugumella burubaensis
items.basis: A fertile early land plant compared with zosterophylls, but retained as incertae sedis in the recent comprehensive phylogenetic treatment.
items.source: [Claisse et al. (2025), Re-evaluating the phylogenetic relationships of zosterophylls](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13274996/)

items.name: Kidstonophyton discoides
items.basis: An antheridiophore-bearing gametophyte associated with Nothia aphylla. The flags describe the associated biological lineage, whose crown-tracheophyte placement remains unresolved.
items.source: [Taylor et al. (2005), Life history biology of early land plants](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC556298/); [Claisse et al. (2025)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13274996/)

items.name: Konioria andrychoviensis
items.basis: Branching axes, reniform sporangia and an exarch conducting strand support its placement among zosterophylls.
items.source: [Zdebska (1982), A new zosterophyll from the Lower Devonian of Poland, abstract](https://881fe75a-0d59-4523-9a92-1143e3e621d1.eurekamag.com/research/004/603/004603075.php)

items.name: Krithodeophyton
items.basis: Branched axes contain protosteles and bear terminal sporangial fructifications. Barinophyte comparisons do not securely resolve its crown lineage.
items.source: [Edwards (1968), A new plant from the Lower Old Red Sandstone of South Wales](https://palass.org/product/1701); [Claisse et al. (2025)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13274996/)

items.name: Langiophyton mackei
items.basis: This denotes the gametophyte usually spelled Langiophyton mackiei, associated with Horneophyton lignieri. The flags describe that non-tracheophyte polysporangiophyte lineage.
items.source: [Taylor et al. (2005), Life history biology of early land plants](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC556298/)

items.name: Leclercqia complexa
items.basis: A herbaceous lycopsid with vascularised divided leaves, exarch xylem and sporophyll-associated sporangia.
items.source: [Banks, Bonamo and Grierson (1972), Leclercqia complexa, a new lycopod from eastern New York](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/003466677290005X)

items.name: Lepidodendropsis
items.basis: A lycopsid stem genus with a complicated history of species delimitation. Published Lower Devonian attributions exist, so its better-known Carboniferous occurrence does not alone justify exclusion.
items.source: [Lejal-Nicol and Massa (1980), Lower Devonian plants of Libya, abstract](https://documentsdelivered.com/source/023/619/023619129.php)

items.name: Leptophloeum australe
items.basis: An arborescent lycopsid, principally documented from Upper Devonian strata. Its broad PBDB age interval needs checking before interpreting it as an early occurrence.
items.source: [New Devonian plant fossil occurrences on the New South Wales South Coast: geological implications](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/330198067_New_Devonian_plant_fossil_occurrences_on_the_New_South_Wales_South_Coast_geological_implications)

items.name: Loganiella canadensis
items.basis: A historical Devonian plant name replacing preoccupied Logania. Its old Psilophytales placement supplies insufficient diagnostic evidence for a modern lineage assignment.
items.source: [Andrews (1970), Index of generic names of fossil plants, p. 122](https://pubs.usgs.gov/bul/1300/report.pdf)

items.name: Loganophyton
items.basis: A genuine Devonian plant genus whose relationships remain unresolved. The consulted research abstract treats it among plants that do not fit established categories.
items.source: [Gensel (2018), The Devonian as a time of major evolutionary innovation and diversification in plants](https://gsa.confex.com/gsa/2018NE/webprogram/Paper310624.html)

items.name: Lycopodia <sp.>
items.basis: Interpreted as an informal lycopod group identification. The flags classify the group denoted; neither the spelling nor the underlying occurrence was independently verified.
items.source: none checked

items.name: Lycopodia ? sp.
items.basis: Interpreted as a tentative informal lycopod identification. The flags classify the denoted group, while the occurrence-level identification remains unverified.
items.source: none checked

items.name: Lycopodia indet.
items.basis: Interpreted as an indeterminate lycopod group identification. This does not establish a genus or independently validate the constituent records.
items.source: none checked

items.name: Lycopodolica sp.
items.basis: Compression axes bear hair-like emergences without demonstrated vascular tissue. Published criticism questions their vascular interpretation, preventing a secure lycophyte assignment.
items.source: [Edwards (1979), A late Silurian flora from south-west Dyfed](https://palass.org/sites/default/files/media/publications/palaeontology/volume_22/vol22_part1_pp23-52.pdf)

items.name: Lycopodolica tsegelnjucki n. sp.
items.basis: The genus has hair-like emergences and possible branching but lacks demonstrated vascular anatomy. A secure polysporangiophyte or lycophyte placement was not established.
items.source: [Edwards (1979), A late Silurian flora from south-west Dyfed](https://palass.org/sites/default/files/media/publications/palaeontology/volume_22/vol22_part1_pp23-52.pdf)

items.name: Lycopodolica tsegelnjuki
items.basis: Apparently a spelling variant of the preceding Lycopodolica identification. The unresolved nomenclature and absence of demonstrated vascular anatomy preclude secure placement.
items.source: [Edwards (1979), A late Silurian flora from south-west Dyfed](https://palass.org/sites/default/files/media/publications/palaeontology/volume_22/vol22_part1_pp23-52.pdf)

items.name: Lycopsida
items.basis: A higher-group identification of lycopsids, members of the lycophyte lineage within crown vascular plants.
items.source: [Xue (2011), Phylogeny of Devonian lycopsids inferred from Bayesian phylogenetic analyses](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/j.1755-6724.2011.00452.x)

items.name: Lyonophyton rhyniensis n. gen. n. sp.
items.basis: The gametophyte associated with Aglaophyton. The flags describe its biological lineage, rather than implying that the preserved gametophyte itself bears sporangia.
items.source: [Taylor et al. (2005), Life history biology of early land plants](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC556298/)

items.name: Macivera gracilis
items.basis: A Late Silurian zosterophyll with branching axes and distally dehiscent sporangia clustered near their tips.
items.source: [Kotyk et al. (2002), Morphologically complex plant macrofossils from the Late Silurian of Arctic Canada](https://bsapubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.3732/ajb.89.6.1004)

items.name: Margophyton
items.basis: Fertile Siberian Margophyton is a zosterophyll with lateral sporangia. Some European axes historically assigned to it instead represent Psilophyton or remain ambiguous.
items.source: [Capel et al., Revisiting the Rebreuve plant assemblage from the Lower Devonian of Artois](https://orbi.uliege.be/bitstream/2268/302489/1/Revisiting%20the%20Rebreuve%20plant%20assemblage%20from%20the%20Lower%20Devonian%20of%20Artois%20northern%20France.pdf)

items.name: Mosellophyton hefteri
items.basis: Originally interpreted as a succulent tracheophyte, these irregularly branching compressions were subsequently combined with Prototaxites. Competing interpretations and inadequate anatomy warrant problematic status.
items.source: [Palaeoenvironment and palaeoecology of intertidal deposits in a Lower Devonian siliciclastic sequence of the Mosel Region](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/233324627_Palaeoenvironment_and_palaeoecology_of_intertidal_deposits_in_a_Lower_Devonian_siliciclastic_sequence_of_the_Mosel_Region_Germany)

items.name: Nemadophyton dechenianum
items.basis: Interpreted as the historical Nematophyton dechenianum, with an apparent spelling error. Described tubular tissue lacks a genuine vascular bundle and has unresolved higher affinity.
items.source: [Historical account of the Elberfeld Middle Devonian flora, Nematophyton dechenianum discussion](https://www.zobodat.at/pdf/Jber-Natwiss-Ver-Elbersfeld_15_0033-0047.pdf)

items.name: Nematasketum diversiforme
items.basis: A nematophyte composed of differently sized tubes and hyphae. Anatomical study supports fungal affinity.
items.source: [Edwards and Axe, Evidence for a fungal affinity for Nematasketum, a close ally of Prototaxites](https://orca.cardiff.ac.uk/id/eprint/15213/)

items.name: Nematophyton
items.basis: The supplied occurrence is Nematophyton taitii, subsequently treated as Prototaxites taiti. Its tubular organisation and disputed higher affinity provide no support for vascular-plant membership.
items.source: [Honegger et al. (2018), Fertile Prototaxites taiti: a basal ascomycete](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5745340/)

items.name: Nematoplexus
items.basis: An enigmatic tubular nematophyte. Plant-like chemical fingerprints do not establish embryophyte identity, sporangial organisation or vascular tissues.
items.source: [Loron et al. (2023), Molecular fingerprints resolve affinities of Rhynie chert organic fossils](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-023-37047-1)

items.name: Nematoplexus rhyniensis
items.basis: A tubular Rhynie nematophyte of debated affinity. Spectroscopic similarity to plant fossilisation products does not demonstrate a polysporangiophyte body plan.
items.source: [Loron et al. (2023), Molecular fingerprints resolve affinities of Rhynie chert organic fossils](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-023-37047-1)

items.name: Nematothallus pseudovasculosa
items.basis: A nematophyte form taxon with cuticular and tubular components. Reconstructed Nematothallus thalli support fungal or lichen-like rather than embryophyte affinity.
items.source: [Edwards, Axe and Honegger (2013), Nematothallus revisited](https://doi.org/10.1111/boj.12119)

items.name: Newspeciesd newspecies
items.basis: Apparently a database placeholder rather than a recoverable botanical name. The fertile-axis organ label does not establish identity or affinity.
items.source: none checked

items.name: Nothia aphylla
items.basis: A branched sporophyte with numerous lateral sporangia. Conducting-cell and dehiscence differences from typical zosterophylls leave its vascular status and crown placement unresolved.
items.source: [Edwards (2003), Embryophytic sporophytes in the Rhynie and Windyfield cherts](https://orca.cardiff.ac.uk/10510/1/Edwards%202003.pdf)

items.name: Odonax borealis n. sp.
items.basis: A zosterophyll with branched, spiny axes and strobili of lateral, reniform, bivalved sporangia.
items.source: [Gerrienne (1996), Lower Devonian plant remains from Marchin: IV. Odonax borealis](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/0034666795001212)

items.name: Oocampsa catheta
items.basis: A branched Devonian plant interpreted as intermediate between trimerophytes and progymnosperms. Both alternatives lie on the euphyllophyte lineage.
items.source: [Wellman and Gensel (2004), Morphology and wall ultrastructure of the spores of Oocampsa catheta, abstract](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/248295329)

items.name: Oricilla bilinearis n. gen. n. sp.
items.basis: A zosterophyll with two rows of lateral reniform sporangia on smooth axes, recovered within Sawdoniaceae in recent phylogenetic analysis.
items.source: [Claisse et al. (2025), Re-evaluating the phylogenetic relationships of zosterophylls](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13274996/)

items.name: Pachytheca
items.basis: Filamentous spheres of conjectural, probably green-algal affinity, without demonstrated embryophyte organisation.
items.source: [Edwards et al. (2026), The nature and affinities of Pachytheca](https://orca.cardiff.ac.uk/id/eprint/187649/)

items.name: Pachytheca ashlayer
items.basis: Classified by the problematic, probably algal genus Pachytheca. The qualifier ashlayer was not verified as a species name.
items.source: [Edwards et al. (2026), The nature and affinities of Pachytheca](https://orca.cardiff.ac.uk/id/eprint/187649/)

items.name: Pachytheca cf. fasciculata
items.basis: A qualified Pachytheca identification retains the genus's problematic, probably algal affinity.
items.source: [Edwards et al. (2026), The nature and affinities of Pachytheca](https://orca.cardiff.ac.uk/id/eprint/187649/)

items.name: Pachytheca indet.
items.basis: Indeterminate Pachytheca represents problematic filamentous spheres, probably green-algal.
items.source: [Edwards et al. (2026), The nature and affinities of Pachytheca](https://orca.cardiff.ac.uk/id/eprint/187649/)

items.name: Pachytheca sp.
items.basis: Unspecified Pachytheca carries the genus's problematic, probably green-algal affinity.
items.source: [Edwards et al. (2026), The nature and affinities of Pachytheca](https://orca.cardiff.ac.uk/id/eprint/187649/)

items.name: Palaeocancellus
items.basis: A calcisphere genus including forms interpreted as altered volvocacean algae. Other assigned forms represent different organisms, preventing a uniform algal assignment.
items.source: [Kaźmierczak (1976), Volvocacean nature of some Palaeozoic non-radiosphaerid calcispheres](https://www.app.pan.pl/archive/published/app21/app21-245.pdf)

items.name: Palaeogeminella folkii
items.basis: Originally assigned to green-algal Ulotrichaceae. This remains provisional because filamentous forms from its Caballos Novaculite provenance have also attracted pseudofossil interpretations.
items.source: [USGS Bulletin 1517, Palaeogeminella entry](https://pubs.usgs.gov/bul/1517/report.pdf); [Edwards and Lyon (1983), Algae from the Rhynie Chert](https://ir.ucc.edu.gh/xmlui/bitstream/handle/123456789/3757/edwards1983.pdf?sequence=1)

items.name: Palaeonitella
items.basis: A charophyte algal genus with anatomically preserved thalli and reproductive structures, outside Embryophyta.
items.source: [Kelman et al. (2003), Charophyte algae from the Rhynie chert](https://doi.org/10.1017/S0263593300000808)

items.name: Palaeonitella cranii
items.basis: An anatomically preserved charophyte with nodal branchlets, antheridia and oogonia.
items.source: [Kelman et al. (2003), Charophyte algae from the Rhynie chert](https://doi.org/10.1017/S0263593300000808)

items.name: Palaeostigma
items.basis: A Devonian axis genus historically compared with lycopsids, but retained incertae sedis in the consulted specimen treatment. Its superficial diagnosis does not securely establish lycophyte or rhyniophyte affinity.
items.source: [Matsumura and Iannuzzi (2015), Plantas devonianas do Brasil e seu significado bioestratigráfico](https://boletimcn.museu-goeldi.br/bcnaturais/en/article/download/490/235/9974)

items.name: Palaeostigma sewardi
items.basis: Incompletely characterised stems belong to a genus historically compared with lycopsids but retained incertae sedis. The PBDB Rhyniaceae placement is insufficiently supported.
items.source: [Matsumura and Iannuzzi (2015), Plantas devonianas do Brasil e seu significado bioestratigráfico](https://boletimcn.museu-goeldi.br/bcnaturais/en/article/download/490/235/9974)

items.name: Paleocuticularia perforata n. gen. n. sp.
items.basis: No diagnostic taxonomic account was recovered. A cuticle occurrence alone cannot establish an embryophyte or vascular-plant parent.
items.source: none checked

items.name: Parka
items.basis: An enigmatic thalloid genus with debated algal and bryophyte comparisons. Its reproductive bodies do not establish a branched polysporangiate sporophyte.
items.source: [Hemsley (1990), Parka decipiens and land plant spore evolution](https://doi.org/10.1080/08912969009386532)

items.name: Parka decipiens
items.basis: A thalloid fossil with alete reproductive bodies compared with algal oospores and bryophyte spores. Its affinity remains enigmatic.
items.source: [Hemsley (1990), Parka decipiens and land plant spore evolution](https://doi.org/10.1080/08912969009386532)

items.name: Pathytheca sp.
items.basis: The exact genus string was not resolved. It may be a transcription of Pachytheca, but the occurrence reference is needed to establish that correction.
items.source: none checked

items.name: Pectinophyton
items.basis: The supplied species P. bipectinatum was transferred to Barinophyton as B. robustius on sporangial architecture. Classification follows that revision and the modern placement of Barinophyton among lycophyte-line barinophytes.
items.source: [Brauer (1980), Barinophyton citrulliforme, abstract including the transfer of P. bipectinatum](https://documentsdelivered.com/source/001/697/001697241.php); [Claisse et al. (2025)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13274996/)

items.name: Perotrilites
items.basis: A dispersed trilete-spore form genus. Its morphology and PBDB Selaginellaceae hierarchy do not independently establish a lycophyte parent.
items.source: [Richardson and Lister (1969), Upper Silurian and Lower Devonian spore assemblages from the Welsh Borderland and South Wales](https://palass.org/sites/default/files/media/publications/palaeontology/volume_12/vol12_part2_pp201-252.pdf)

items.name: Pertica
items.basis: A basal euphyllophyte genus with organised lateral branching and terminal sporangial clusters. The supplied P. dalhousii is a recognised trimerophyte.
items.source: [Doran, Gensel and Andrews (1978), New occurrences of trimerophytes from the Devonian of eastern Canada](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/237160469_New_occurrences_of_trimerophytes_from_the_Devonian_of_eastern_Canada)

items.name: Pertica varia
items.basis: Explicitly treated as a species of the trimerophyte genus Pertica. Its fertile branching systems and in situ spores support basal euphyllophyte affinity.
items.source: [Noetinger, Strayer and Tomescu (2018), Spore wall ultrastructure and development in a basal euphyllophyte, comparative discussion](https://bsapubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/pdfdirect/10.1002/ajb2.1137)

items.name: Pertonella dactylethra n. gen. n. sp.
items.basis: A late Silurian rhyniophytoid with Cooksonia-like terminal sporangia distinguished by spiny projections. Crown-tracheophyte anatomy is not established.
items.source: [Fanning, Richardson and Edwards (1991), A review of in situ spores in Silurian land plants](https://doi.org/10.1093/oso/9780198577461.003.0003)

items.name: Pinakodendron
items.basis: The original account assigns the supplied P. corneti from Belgian Early Devonian rocks to a lycopod genus. The sterile material warrants moderate confidence in that attribution.
items.source: [Ledoux-Marcelle (1930), Sur les flores du Dévonien de la Belgique: II. Pinakodendron corneti](https://biblio.naturalsciences.be/rbins-publications/bulletin-de-la-societe-belge-de-geologie/040%20-%201930/bsbg_040_1930_pv_10-21.pdf)
